name: Suspension disc insulator
summary: A porcelain disc with an iron cap and a steel pin. A string of such discs, each linked to the next, hangs a power line from a tower and grows with the voltage.
how: Fire a porcelain disc about 255 mm across with a deep rain skirt on the lower face.
Cement a cast iron cap on top and a steel pin in the hollow of the disc.
Link the discs pin to cap in a string, and add one disc for each 10 to 15 kV of line voltage.
Test each disc with high voltage before use.

origin.note: Engineers at a US electric company make the first cap-and-pin porcelain disc for a string on high-voltage lines.

adoptions.via: Porcelain works make the glazed disc of the string, and the string replaces the rigid pin insulator on high-voltage lines.
